title: After a deploy, order emails stopped and nothing alarmed

objective: Read configuration from process.env and --env-file, and exit with a meaningful code on failure

sources.cite: Node.js v26.13.1 API, Command-line options: --env-file and --env-file-if-exists
sources.note: Relevant text: --env-file 'Loads environment variables from a file ... making them available to applications on process.env'; 'If the same variable is defined in the environment and in the file, the value from the environment takes precedence'; 'An error is thrown if the file does not exist.' --env-file-if-exists: 'Behavior is the same as --env-file, but an error is not thrown if the file does not exist.' Both 'no longer experimental' since v24.10.0 and v22.21.0. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (the first 100,000 characters, which held both sections).

sources.cite: Node.js v26.13.1 API, process: process.exit() and process.exitCode
sources.note: Relevant text: process.exit(): 'If code is omitted, exit uses either the 'success' code 0 or the value of process.exitCode if it has been set'; 'Rather than calling process.exit() directly, the code should set the process.exitCode and allow the process to exit naturally'; an uncaught exception exits 'with code 1' by default. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (the first 100,000 characters; the Exit codes section was not reached).

Relevant text: 'If set to on-failure, the service will be restarted when the process exits with a non-zero exit code', is terminated by a signal, or times out; in the page's table a 'Clean exit code or signal' restarts only under always and on-success. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Why a service that exits 0 on a missing setting is not restarted and is not reported as failed. The journal and systemctl output in the scenario are authored renderings in the tools' style.

brief.situation: You are the on-call engineer at Fernhill Books, a fictional online bookshop. The notifier service, a Node.js 26 LTS program run by systemd, sends order confirmation emails from a queue. Release 3.8.0 went out at 14:02. At 14:30 support reports missing confirmations, yet no alert fired. Queued emails expire after 60 minutes, so the oldest start to expire at 15:02. Find out why the service is not sending, get it sending again without losing mail, and make sure the next failure of this kind is loud.
handover: notifier reads SMTP_URL and other settings from process.env. The release also renamed its environment file.
Monitoring alerts when a systemd unit is in the failed state; the unit has Restart=on-failure.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The incident keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, service or job and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command or change takes, and when the fictional incident develops, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The queue's 60-minute message lifetime makes the 14:02 emails expire at 15:02, 32 minutes after the report.

writeup.question: For the incident record: why the service stopped without any alert, how you got mail flowing without losing any, and what makes the next missing setting loud.

parts.label: Why it was silent
parts.criteria: Explains that --env-file-if-exists skips a missing file without error, so SMTP_URL was absent from process.env, and that process.exit() with no code exits 0, which Restart=on-failure does not restart and monitoring of failed units does not see.
parts.modelAnswer: The release renamed the env file. The unit used --env-file-if-exists=/etc/notifier/env, which quietly loads nothing when the file is missing, so process.env.SMTP_URL was undefined. config.ts then called process.exit() with no code, which is exit 0: systemd treated it as success, did not restart it and never marked it failed.

parts.label: Restoring without loss
parts.criteria: Points the unit at the right file, reloads systemd before restarting, checks the queue drains; never purges the queue.
parts.modelAnswer: I changed the unit to --env-file=/etc/notifier/notifier.env, ran daemon-reload, restarted, and watched the queue drain to 0 with every waiting confirmation sent.

parts.label: Making it loud
parts.criteria: Uses --env-file (which errors on a missing file) and/or exits with a non-zero code (process.exitCode = 1 or a thrown error) on missing required settings.
parts.modelAnswer: --env-file fails at startup if the file is missing, and 3.8.1 sets process.exitCode = 1 on a missing setting. Either way systemd marks the unit failed and monitoring alerts.

expertPath.text: systemctl status: inactive (dead), status=0/SUCCESS, so on-failure never restarted it. journalctl: SMTP_URL not set, clean exit.
systemctl cat and ls /etc/notifier: the unit loads /etc/notifier/env with --env-file-if-exists; the release renamed it notifier.env.
Point the unit at notifier.env with --env-file (it fails loudly if the file goes missing), daemon-reload, restart, and watch the queue drain.
Ship 3.8.1, which throws on a missing setting so Node.js exits with code 1, and record both silent paths.

restored.headline: Good: restored and made loud
restored.body: A clean exit hid the failure from systemd and monitoring. You loaded the renamed file with --env-file, drained the queue, and made the next missing setting fail the unit.

restoredGaps.headline: Sending again, with gaps
restoredGaps.body: Mail flows. The criteria show the gaps: still silent on the next missing file, late, restarted blind, or the drain never checked.

purgedQueue.headline: Order emails deleted
purgedQueue.body: The queue was the one thing working as designed: it held the mail until the notifier came back. Fix the consumer; keep the messages.

expired.headline: The emails expired
expired.body: The journal said what was wrong within two minutes: no SMTP_URL, clean exit. The renamed file was one ls away.

stillDown.headline: Closed too soon
stillDown.body: A restart with nothing changed exits 0 again. Fix where the settings come from, reload systemd, then restart.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The unit loaded /etc/notifier/env with --env-file-if-exists, which loads nothing and says nothing when the file is missing; the release renamed it notifier.env, so SMTP_URL was undefined. The code then called process.exit() with no code, exit 0, which Restart=on-failure does not restart and which never puts the unit in the failed state that monitoring watches. Point the unit at the file with --env-file (which errors if it is missing), daemon-reload, restart and watch the queue drain; then exit with a non-zero code on any missing required setting. Never purge the queue.
